basis: Quantifiers: for every odd prime p, d(UT_3(F_p)) = 3p-3. Volkmann arXiv:2608.18651v1 (2026-08-19) abstract claims a uniform proof of d(H_{p^3})=3p-3 for all odd p (order-value growth theorem plus Cauchy-Davenport). Also p=7 by arXiv:2608.13747v1; Qu-Wang arXiv:2608.23319v2 cites the general result. Bodies not read; correctness not audited.
statement: Godara and Sarkar conjectured that, for every odd prime $p$, if $H_{p^3}=\operatorname{UT}_3(\mathbb{F}_p)$ is the Heisenberg group of order $p^3$, then $\mathsf{d}(H_{p^3})=3p-3$, where $\mathsf{d}(G)$ is the maximum length of a sequence over a finite group $G$ having no nonempty subsequence whose terms can be ordered to have product equal to the identity.
title: Godara–Sarkar conjecture for the small Davenport constant of Heisenberg groups

basis: Determine TD(16). Silva-Kowada-Rocco-Walter arXiv:2609.17493v3 abstract claims a proof of TD(16)=9 by exhaustive twisted-bracelet verification. Wording defect: for ordinary transpositions the literal reading gives the trivial value n-1=15; the intended object is block transposition (SBT). A wording correction carries no credit.
statement: For a permutation $\pi\in S_n$, let $d_T(\pi,\iota)$ be the minimum number of transpositions whose product sends $\pi$ to the identity permutation $\iota$. Define the transposition diameter by $TD(n)=\max_{\pi\in S_n}d_T(\pi,\iota)$. Determine the exact value of $TD(16)$. The cited preprint claims that $TD(16)=9$.
title: Transposition diameter problem

basis: Single instance: alpha(frb100-40). Ugurlu arXiv:2609.02804v1 gives a 100-vertex independent set plus a partition into 100 cliques of size 40. Together these settle alpha=100. Certificate not downloaded or rechecked.
statement: Let $G_{\mathrm{frb100\text{-}40}}=(V,E)$ be the publicly specified $4{,}000$-vertex Model-RB benchmark graph. Determine its independence number $\alpha(G_{\mathrm{frb100\text{-}40}})$, equivalently find a set $S\subseteq V$ of maximum cardinality such that for all distinct $u,v\in S$, $\{u,v\}\notin E$. The reported certificate claims that $\alpha(G_{\mathrm{frb100\text{-}40}})=100$.
title: Model-RB frb100-40 maximum-independent-set challenge

basis: For every A subset N with ab+1 non-squarefree for all a,b in A: upper density <= 1/25. erdosproblems.com/848 (edited 2025-12-06; fetched 2026-10-31) records Sawhney's theorem: there is c>0 such that, for large N, if |A|>=(1/25-c)N then A lies in 7 or 18 mod 25. The density bound follows at once. A cap [1,N] inherits the property; if limsup > 1/25, infinitely many N give a single class of size <= N/25+1, a contradiction. Sawhney note body not read.
statement: Determine whether the following sharp upper-density bound holds: if $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ satisfies $ab+1$ is not squarefree for every $a,b\in A$, then $\overline{d}(A):=\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{|A\cap\{1,\ldots,N\}|}{N}\leq\frac{1}{25}$. The bound is sharp, since $A=\{n\in\mathbb{N}:n\equiv 7\pmod{25}\}$ satisfies $ab+1\equiv 0\pmod{25}$ for all $a,b\in A$.
title: Erdős Problem 848

basis: For all n>=8 with n = 0 mod 4: H_5(n;5) exists. Mella arXiv:2609.24399v1 constructs one for every n>=12 with n = 0 mod 4; n=8 and n=16 were earlier sporadic examples. Body not read.
statement: Determine whether a square integer relative Heffter array $\mathrm{H}_5(n;5)$ exists for every integer $n\ge 8$ satisfying $n\equiv 0\pmod{4}$. The 2026 source claims an affirmative answer: such arrays exist for $n=8$ and for every $n\ge 12$ with $n\equiv 0\pmod{4}$.
title: Integer relative Heffter-array existence problem

basis: For all n>=13: gamma(F_2(P_n))=d(n). The record leaves c_n unspecified (statement incomplete). Acosta Troncoso-Rivera arXiv:2610.11265v1 claims the full result: earlier upper bound plus a computer-assisted lower bound in the Goncalves-Pinlou-Rao-Thomasse style.
statement: For every integer $n\ge 13$, determine whether the domination number of the $2$-token graph of the path graph $P_n$ satisfies $\gamma(F_2(P_n))=d(n)$, where $d(n)=\frac{1}{10}(n^2+5n+c_n)$ and $c_n$ is the explicitly specified constant determined by $n\bmod 5$.
title: Leaños–Acosta Troncoso–Rivera 2-token path domination conjecture

basis: QMA vs QCMA, a major complexity-class separation. No bounded certificate mechanism.
statement:
Determine whether QMA=QCMA: does every language decidable by a polynomial-time quantum verifier using a polynomial-size quantum witness also admit a polynomial-time quantum verification protocol using only a polynomial-size classical witness?

Source: [John Bostanci, Jonas Haferkamp, Chinmay Nirkhe, and Mark Zhandry, Separating QMA from QCMA with a classical oracle, Introduction](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2025/176/revision/1/download/).

Status Open · subcases solved Status review date not recorded in this edition

Listed by [ProofAtlas](https://www.proofatlas.ai/open-problems/#problem-qma-versus-qcma-problem). Status qualification is attributed to ProofAtlas; no full resolution is certified here.
title: QMA versus QCMA Problem

basis: For each k>=1: the least n>=k with prod_{j=0..k}(n-j) | C(2n,n). Uniform existence and determination are open (Erdos #396). Computing per-k values only yields parameter instances.
statement: For each integer $k\ge 1$, determine the smallest integer $n\ge k$ such that $n(n-1)(n-2)\cdots(n-k)$ divides the central binomial coefficient $\binom{2n}{n}$; equivalently, determine $n_k=\min\{n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge k}:\prod_{j=0}^{k}(n-j)\mid\binom{2n}{n}\}$ whenever this set is nonempty.
title: Erdős problem #396

basis: Exact (phi_S, rho_S) region. Ansari-Rockel arXiv:2608.20176v1 claims the max rho given the footrule via an optimal-transport dual certificate, completing the region. Body not read.
statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the set of bivariate copulas, equivalently the set of joint laws of random variables $U,V\sim\mathcal{U}(0,1)$. Define Spearman's rho and Spearman's footrule by $\rho_S(U,V)=12\mathbb{E}[UV]-3$ and $\phi_S(U,V)=1-6\mathbb{E}[|U-V|]$. Determine exactly the attainable region $\mathcal{R}=\{(\phi_S(U,V),\rho_S(U,V)):(U,V)\text{ has a bivariate copula law}\}$. Equivalently, for every $x\in[-\tfrac12,1]$, determine the extremal values, in particular $\sup\{\rho_S(U,V):\phi_S(U,V)=x\}$, and hence the exact upper and lower boundaries of $\mathcal{R}$.
title: Spearman rho–footrule region problem

basis: For all 1<=k<=n: real-rootedness classification of a_{n,k} and |b_{n,k}| (Bona et al. Conjecture 36). The record's own source (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.22660798) reports the counterexample (n,k)=(3,3). It also publicly proposes a boundary-corrected classification with a candidate proof. A corrected-domain version would be a wording/domain correction of a publicly treated question: no credit. Zenodo not fetched.
statement: For every pair of integers $1\le k\le n$, consider the refined Narayana polynomial and its formal degree-$k$ symmetric decomposition, written in the form $F_{n,k}(t)=a_{n,k}(t)+t\,b_{n,k}(t)$. The problem is to determine exactly for which pairs $(n,k)$ the polynomials $a_{n,k}(t)$ and the coefficientwise absolute-value polynomial $|b_{n,k}(t)|$ are real-rooted, according to Conjecture 36 of Bóna et al. The supplied source reports that the published classification fails at $(n,k)=(3,3)$: there $a_{3,3}(t)=(1+t)(1+t^2)$ and $|b_{3,3}(t)|=1+t+t^2$, neither of which is real-rooted. A boundary-corrected classification has been proposed, but its general proof has not been independently verified.
title: Real-rootedness classification for refined Narayana polynomials

basis: Polynomial-time distribution-free PAC learning of s-term DNF. A long-standing learning-theory problem with no bounded mechanism.
statement:
Given an unknown s-term DNF f on {0,1}^n and random labeled examples drawn from an arbitrary unknown distribution D, construct a possibly improper hypothesis in time polynomial in n, s, 1/epsilon, and log(1/delta) whose D-error is at most epsilon with probability at least 1-delta.

Source: [Alman, Nadimpalli, Patel, and Servedio, DNF Learning via Locally Mixing Random Walks, Section 1.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2505.18839v1).

Status Open · subcases solved Status review date not recorded in this edition

Listed by [ProofAtlas](https://www.proofatlas.ai/open-problems/#problem-polynomial-time-distribution-free-pac-learning-of-dnf-formulas). Status qualification is attributed to ProofAtlas; no full resolution is certified here.
title: Polynomial-Time Distribution-Free PAC Learning of DNF Formulas

basis: Q(D_p) for every p in [0,1]. Superadditivity barrier; long-standing. No bounded mechanism.
statement:
For every p in [0,1], determine the exact unassisted quantum capacity Q(D_p) of the memoryless qubit channel D_p(rho)=(1-p)rho+pI/2. Capacity is the supremum of asymptotically achievable rates in qubits per channel use for quantum-information transmission with vanishing error and arbitrary block coding, without preshared entanglement or auxiliary classical communication.

Source: [Quantum Information chapter10, 2025 snapshot](https://www.preskill.caltech.edu/ph219/chap10_6A_2025.pdf).

Status Open · subcases solved Status review date not recorded in this edition

Listed by [ProofAtlas](https://www.proofatlas.ai/open-problems/#problem-depolarizing-channel-capacity). Status qualification is attributed to ProofAtlas; no full resolution is certified here.
title: Exact Unassisted Quantum Capacity of the Qubit Depolarizing Channel

basis: Least number of variables for undecidable H10 over Z. The gap between known decidable and undecidable variable counts is a deep open problem.
statement:
Determine the least integer n for which no algorithm decides whether an arbitrary integer-coefficient polynomial in at most n variables has an integer zero.

Source: [William Gasarch, Hilbert's Tenth Problem: Refinements and Variants (2021), Notation 3.1 and Theorems 4.1-4.2.](https://www.cs.umd.edu/users/gasarch/open/hilbert10openproblems.pdf).

Status Open · subcases solved Status review date not recorded in this edition

Listed by [ProofAtlas](https://www.proofatlas.ai/open-problems/#problem-smallest-number-of-variables-for-undecidable-hilbert-s-tenth-problem-over-z). Status qualification is attributed to ProofAtlas; no full resolution is certified here.
title: Smallest number of variables for undecidable Hilbert's Tenth Problem over Z

basis: Which APs n=r mod m have ou*(n)=0 mod 4 for all n; in particular the moduli 50/98/242 enlargements. Banerjee-Ghosh Dastidar arXiv:2610.20135v1 (PDF sha 3f1760fc..., derived text lines 95-175). Problem 1.3 is answered by Thm 1.5 (complete mod-4 classification for odd n) and Cor 1.7/1.8 (moduli 2l^2): 50 gives {37,47}; 98 gives {47,61,89}; 242 gives ten residues. Hand evaluation of Cor 1.8 and a bounded computation for n<=8000 (runs/oustar.r2.json) agree exactly; evidence, not proof. The literal 'determine which APs' also covers even n, which Thm 1.5 does not classify. In the tested moduli no even-residue AP appeared up to 8000. The residual is a method adaptation and was not pursued.
statement: Let $\operatorname{ou}^{*}(n)$ denote the number of odd strongly unimodal sequences of size $n$. Determine which arithmetic progressions $n\equiv r\pmod m$ satisfy $\operatorname{ou}^{*}(n)\equiv 0\pmod 4$ for every $n\equiv r\pmod m$. In particular, determine whether the computationally suggested enlargements of the known progressions with moduli $100$, $196$, and $484$ to moduli $50$, $98$, and $242$, respectively, satisfy this divisibility condition.
title: Bringmann–Lovejoy problem on odd strongly unimodal sequences

basis: Determine h(n); prove h(n)>n^{1+c} (Erdos #956, convex translates). A hard incidence-geometry problem. Live status not checked.
statement: If $C,D\subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ then the distance between $C$ and $D$ is defined by $ \delta(C,D)=\inf_{\substack{c\in C\\ d\in D}}\| c-d\|. $ Let $h(n)$ be the maximal number of unit distances between disjoint convex translates. That is, the maximal $m$ such that there is a compact convex set $C\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ and a set $X$ of size $n$ such that all $(C+x)_{x\in X}$ are disjoint and there are $m$ pairs $x_1,x_2\in X$ such that $ \delta(C+x_1,C+x_2)=1. $ Determine $h(n)$ - in particular, prove that there exists a constant $c>0$ such that $h(n)>n^{1+c}$ for all large $n$.
title: Erdős Problem #956 — If $C,D\subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ then the distance between $C$ and $D$ is defined by $ \delta(C,D)=\inf_{\substack{c\in C\\ d\in D}}\| c-d\|. $ Let $h(n)$ be the maximal number of unit distances between…

basis: If |P(s)|=1, every non-square n in N(Delta) with squarefree part s has a unique Delta-primitive decomposition. The record's reference field says 'refuted according to the source' (Schvollner arXiv:2605.25264). The arXiv abstract does not mention it and the body was not read. A source-internal refutation would carry no credit in any case.
statement: Let $s\in\mathbb{N}$ be square-free, and let $P(s)$ be the set of $\Delta$-primitives with square-free part $s$. A natural number $n$ has a **$\Delta$-primitive decomposition** if it can be written as $n=\alpha^2m$ with $\alpha\in\mathbb{N}$ and $m$ $\Delta$-primitive. **Fixed-square-free-part uniqueness conjecture.** If $|P(s)|=1$, then every non-square $n\in\mathbb{N}(\Delta)$ with square-free part $s$ admits a unique $\Delta$-primitive decomposition. The conjecture refines a uniqueness question that is false in general: the paper gives $5616=3^2\cdot624=2^2\cdot1404$ as the smallest counterexample, while the classification of integers with multiple decompositions remains open.
title: Uniqueness of the -primitive decomposition for fixed square-free part

basis: WOWII Conjecture 160: for connected G, L_s(G) >= max l(v) + max T(v)*chi_{C4}(G). The record itself states that a formal proof and an independent second proof were recorded in a public pull request. Not fetched (GitHub route restricted).
statement: WOWII [Conjecture 160](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/) For a simple connected graph $G$, $L_s(G) \ge \max_v l(v) + \max_v T(v) \cdot \chi_{C_4}(G)$ where: - $L_s(G) = \mathrm{SimpleGraph.Ls}\, G$ is the maximum number of leaves over all spanning trees of $G$, - $\max_v l(v)$ is the maximum local independence number over vertices, - $\max_v T(v)$ is the maximum number of triangles incident to any vertex, - $\chi_{C_4}(G)$ is `1` if $G$ has no cycle of length four and `0` otherwise. A formal proof uses the $C_4$-free neighborhood identity $d(v) = \lambda(v) + T(v)$ with a star/geodesic case analysis, routed through the connected-seed spanning-tree bound developed for Conjecture 2. An independent second proof, via a closest maximizer pair joined by a shortest path, is linked from the pull request that recorded the solution.
title: WoTW 160

basis: For all planar G: a(G) >= n/2 (Albertson-Berman). Refuted: Makarov arXiv:2608.13964v1 gives a 39-vertex planar graph with a(G)=19, and cites an earlier AI-assisted counterexample.
statement: For every simple planar graph $G$ with $n=|V(G)|$ vertices, if $a(G)$ denotes the maximum number of vertices in an induced forest of $G$, then $a(G)\geq \frac{n}{2}$.
title: Albertson–Berman conjecture on induced forests in planar graphs

basis: For all n and 2<p<inf: e(l_p^n)=n+1 (Kusner). Refuted: Chalmers arXiv:2608.14013v2 gives 58 equilateral points in l_5^56, certified in exact arithmetic.
statement: For every integer $n\geq 1$ and every real $p$ satisfying $2<p<\infty$, the maximum cardinality of an equilateral set in $\ell_p^n$ is $e(\ell_p^n)=n+1$. Equivalently, every set $X\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ whose distinct points have pairwise $\ell_p$-distance $1$ has at most $n+1$ elements.
title: Kusner’s conjecture on equilateral sets in ℓ_p^n

basis: The record does not define h, H or the claimed normal orders (it says so itself). The source is a GitHub repository (restricted route). No literal statement to assess.
statement: Determine the normal orders of the arithmetic functions $h(n)$ and $H(n)$. The supplied source identifies this as Erdős Problem $\#696$, but does not define $h$, $H$, or specify the claimed normal-order functions precisely enough to state the conjecture in full.
title: Erdős Problem #696 (normal-order conjecture)

basis: For all connected G with Delta<=3: gamma <= 2rho+1. Refuted: Huh-Kim arXiv:2608.15525v1 explicit families with gamma=26*2^t-4 and rho=12*2^t-2, giving unbounded additive violation (also cubic).
statement: For every connected graph $G$ with maximum degree $\Delta(G)\le 3$, the domination number satisfies $\gamma(G)\le 2\rho(G)+1$, where $\rho(G)$ is the maximum cardinality of a set of vertices whose pairwise distances are at least $3$.
title: Domination–packing inequality $\gamma(G)\le2\rho(G)+1$

basis: Bickle's k-collapsible minimum formula for all k>=3, n>=k+1. Zhan arXiv:2608.15629v1 claims a proof.
statement: For every pair of integers $k\ge 3$ and $n\ge k+1$, the minimum of $\left|\{v\in V(G):\deg_G(v)=k\}\right|$ over all graphs $G$ of order $n$ satisfying $\delta(G)=k$ and $\delta(H)<k$ for every nonempty proper induced subgraph $H$ of $G$ is $\max\left\{\left\lceil\frac{2n}{2k-1}\right\rceil,\,k^2-k-2-(k-3)n\right\}$, where such a graph is called $k$-collapsible.
title: Bickle’s conjecture on collapsible graphs

basis: Exists n>24 with max_{m<n}(m+tau(m)) <= n+2? Mian-Siddique arXiv:2608.17880v1 give a kernel-checked exclusion to 1e9 only. Computation excludes up to about 9e18; the asymptotic step is open. No full-scope mechanism.
statement: Determine whether there exists an integer $n>24$ such that $\max_{1\le m<n}\bigl(m+\tau(m)\bigr)\le n+2$, where $\tau(m)$ denotes the number of positive divisors of $m$. Equivalently, the conjecture asserts that no such $n$ exists.
title: Erdős problem 647

basis: For all large n: f(n,4)=2n-4? Zak arXiv:2608.17727v1 proves only 2n-10n^{2/3}-7 < f(n,4) <= 2n-4, so the exact value is open. Metadata discrepancy: the record names Keevash-Sudakov, but the arXiv author is Andrzej Zak.
statement: For an $n$-vertex graph $G$ and a permutation $\sigma$ of its vertex set, define $I_G(\sigma)=|E(G)\cap E(\sigma(G))|$, and let $f(n,4)$ be the minimum possible value of $|E(G)|$ over all $n$-vertex graphs satisfying $I_G(\sigma)\ge 4$ for every permutation $\sigma$. The problem asks whether, for all sufficiently large integers $n$, $f(n,4)=2n-4$.
title: Erdős four-edge intersection problem

basis: Albertson-Berman again (duplicate theme of 382983). Refuted: arXiv:2608.17350v1 gives a 31-vertex triangulation with a=15 and a 15/31 family. Metadata discrepancy: the record names Eppstein-Karpov, but the arXiv author is Heejae Jung.
statement: For every simple planar graph $G$ with $n=|V(G)|$ vertices, there exists a set $S\subseteq V(G)$ such that the induced subgraph $G[S]$ is a forest and $|S|\ge n/2$. Equivalently, if $a(G)$ denotes the maximum number of vertices in an induced forest of $G$, then $a(G)\ge n/2$.
title: Albertson–Berman conjecture

basis: For all n>=4: 2-connected G with delta >= sqrt(3n) has 2-connected subgraphs of every order 4..n (Kashima). Ozeki-Ueoro arXiv:2608.17478v2 prove delta >= 2n^{2/3}+6n^{1/3}+2 only. Screening idea checked: the order-4 obstruction (C4-free) dies because delta(delta-1) <= n-1 forces delta < sqrt(3n). No small-counterexample mechanism was identified.
statement: For every integer $n\ge 4$, every $2$-connected graph $G$ of order $n$ with minimum degree $\delta(G)\ge \sqrt{3n}$ contains a $2$-connected subgraph of every order $\ell\in\{4,5,\ldots,n\}$.
title: Kashima’s pancyclicity analogue conjecture

basis: For each n>=2: does det D^2u >= delta with u in W^{2,n}_loc imply Du open and discrete? Zhong arXiv:2608.16757v2 gives a negative answer for every n>=4. The critical exponent p_{n,1}=n(n-1)/2 exceeds n only when n>3, so n=3 (critical) and n=2 are not settled by the abstract. This is a hard PDE residual with no bounded mechanism.
statement: For each dimension $n\ge 2$, determine whether the following implication holds: for every domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{n}$, every $u\in W^{2,n}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, and every constant $\delta>0$, if $\det D^{2}u\ge\delta$ almost everywhere in $\Omega$, then the gradient mapping $Du:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^{n}$ is open and discrete.
title: Guerra–Tione Question 5.5 on gradient mappings

basis: Universal C with sigma_k(G,B) <= C d_max (g+k)/|B|. Zhan-Zhou arXiv:2608.17264v1 claims a proof and sharpness, resolving Lin-Zhao.
statement: Does there exist a universal constant $C>0$ such that, for every connected graph $G=(V,E)$ with boundary $B$, maximum degree $d_{\max}$, and genus $g$, one has $\sigma_k(G,B)\leq C d_{\max}\frac{g+k}{|B|}$ for every integer $k$ satisfying $1\leq k\leq |B|$, where $\sigma_k(G,B)$ is the $k$-th Steklov eigenvalue of $G$ with boundary $B$?
title: Lin–Zhao graph Steklov eigenvalue problem

basis: Exact R(4,20). Yu arXiv:2608.18169v2 gives only the lower bound 252. The exact value is far beyond bounded certificates.
statement: Determine the exact value of the Ramsey number $R(4,20)$, defined by $R(4,20)=\min\{n\in\mathbb{N}:\text{ every graph on }n\text{ vertices contains either a copy of }K_4\text{ or an independent set of }20\text{ vertices}\}$.
title: Ramsey number R(4,20)

basis: sum_j delta_f(H_j)^{1/3} < inf. Du-Xie arXiv:2608.20216v1 claims a proof.
statement: Determine whether, for every countable family of hyperplanes $\{H_j\}_{j\in\mathbb{N}}$ in general position in $\mathbb{P}^m$ and every linearly nondegenerate holomorphic curve $f\colon\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{P}^m$ of finite lower order, the Nevanlinna defects satisfy $\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\delta_f(H_j)^{1/3}<\infty$.
title: Endpoint Nevanlinna defect problem

basis: For all connected G: gamma_b <= 2mp. Islam arXiv:2608.20036v2 claims a constructive proof.
statement: For every connected graph $G$, the broadcast domination number is at most twice the multipacking number: $\gamma_b(G)\leq 2\operatorname{mp}(G)$, where $\gamma_b(G)$ is the minimum cost of a dominating broadcast on $G$ and $\operatorname{mp}(G)$ is the maximum cardinality of a multipacking in $G$.
title: Broadcast domination conjecture

basis: Lichiardopol conjecture. Albrechtsen-Steiner arXiv:2608.20012v1 claim a proof in full generality.
statement: $\exists g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}\ \forall k\in\mathbb{N}\ \forall D\ \bigl(\delta^+(D)\ge g(k)\ \Longrightarrow\ \exists C_1,\ldots,C_k\text{ vertex-disjoint directed cycles in }D\text{ such that }|C_i|\ne|C_j|\text{ for all }i\ne j\bigr)$, where $\delta^+(D)$ denotes the minimum out-degree of $D$.
title: Lichiardopol’s conjecture

basis: For every eps>0 there is a non-synchronizing G with delta >= (3/4-eps)n. Lepsveridze-Zhang arXiv:2608.20010v1 prove an absolute eta>0 such that delta >= (3/4-eta)n implies global synchronization, so the statement is false for eps<eta.
statement: For every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a finite simple graph $G$ on $n$ vertices such that $\delta(G)\geq (3/4-\varepsilon)n$ and $G$ is not globally synchronizing for the Kuramoto model; equivalently, the Kuramoto energy on $G$ has a local minimum other than a fully synchronized state.
title: Bandeira–Kireeva–Maillard–Rödder Kuramoto conjecture

basis: For all k>=2: D(k)=gcd_{2<=q<=k+1} C(qk,k)=1 iff (k+1)/ppart(k+1) > ppart(k+1). Guo-Qiu-Cao-Feng-Gao arXiv:2606.22997v1 (2026-06-22) prove exactly this criterion, with a Lean formalization accepted into Formal Conjectures (per abstract). OEIS A080170 comment dated 2026-06-29 agrees. D(k) was confirmed from the abstract; body not read.
statement: For every integer $k\ge 2$, the binomial-coefficient gcd quantity $D(k)$ specified in OEIS A080170 satisfies $D(k)=1$ if and only if $\frac{k+1}{\operatorname{ppart}(k+1)}>\operatorname{ppart}(k+1)$, where $\operatorname{ppart}(n)=\max\{p^a:p\text{ is prime and }p^a\mathrel{\|}n\}$ is the largest exact prime-power component of $n$.
title: OEIS A080170 conjecture

basis: Henning-Yeo identifying vertex cover bound (the record leaves the inequality unspecified). Wang arXiv:2608.19455v2 refutes it for every Delta>=4 with unbounded gaps.
statement: For every finite graph $G$ with order $n=|V(G)|$, size $m=|E(G)|$, and maximum degree $\Delta=\Delta(G)$, does the identifying vertex cover number of $G$ satisfy the upper-bound inequality conjectured by Henning and Yeo in terms of $n$, $m$, and $\Delta$?
title: Henning–Yeo conjecture on identifying vertex covers

basis: Minimum superpermutation length for every n>5. A known hard open problem with no bounded mechanism.
statement: A superpermutation on $n$ symbols is a string containing every permutation of the $n$ symbols as a contiguous substring. Determine the minimum possible length of a superpermutation for every $n>5$.
title: Minimum length of a superpermutation

basis: P(G,k)=P_l(G,k)>0 implies equality at k+1. Zhang-Dong arXiv:2608.19773v2 construct infinite counterexample families for every k>=3.
statement: For every finite graph $G$ and every integer $k\ge 1$, if $P(G,k)=P_{\ell}(G,k)>0$, then $P(G,k+1)=P_{\ell}(G,k+1)$, where $P(G,k)$ is the number of proper $k$-colorings of $G$ and $P_{\ell}(G,k)=\min_{L}|\{\text{proper }L\text{-colorings of }G\}|$ is the minimum, over all assignments $L$ of lists of $k$ colors to the vertices of $G$, of the number of proper $L$-colorings.
title: Chromatic-polynomial/list-color-function persistence conjecture

basis: Generalized rational exponents conjecture. Hou-Yang arXiv:2608.19923v1 claim a proof.
statement: For every rational number $\alpha\ge 1$, there exist fixed finite simple graphs $H_\alpha$ and $F_\alpha$ such that, as $n\to\infty$, the maximum number of copies of $H_\alpha$ in an $n$-vertex graph containing no copy of $F_\alpha$ satisfies $\operatorname{ex}(n,H_\alpha,F_\alpha)=\Theta(n^\alpha)$.
title: Generalized rational exponents conjecture

basis: Exact gr(Av(1324)). Norton arXiv:2608.20292v3 gives only a lower bound. Famous open problem.
statement: Determine the exact value of the Stanley–Wilf limit $\operatorname{gr}(\operatorname{Av}(1324)):=\lim_{n\to\infty}\lvert\operatorname{Av}_n(1324)\rvert^{1/n}$, where $\operatorname{Av}_n(1324)$ is the set of permutations of length $n$ containing no subsequence order-isomorphic to the pattern $1324$.
title: Growth rate of Av(1324)

basis: M(Q_K) = H^inf cap Q_K^log? The record leaves Q_K^log unspecified. Cao-Jiang-Li arXiv:2608.20205v1 claim a complete non-testing characterization of M(Q_K) answering Bao-Wulan. Whether the answer is yes or no is not visible in the abstract; either way it is publicly addressed. Body not read.
statement: For the Möbius-invariant space $Q_K$ on the unit disc, determine whether the pointwise multiplier algebra satisfies $\mathcal{M}(Q_K)=H^\infty\cap Q_K^{\log}$, where $\mathcal{M}(Q_K)=\{g:g f\in Q_K\text{ for every }f\in Q_K\text{ and }f\mapsto gf\text{ is bounded on }Q_K\}$ and $Q_K^{\log}$ is the logarithmic $Q_K$-class specified in the Bao–Wulan formulation.
title: Bao–Wulan multiplier problem for QK spaces

basis: For every finite nonabelian G: E(G)=d(G)+|G| (Gao-Zhuang). Qu-Wang arXiv:2608.23319v2 settle groups of order p^3 only. The general conjecture is open with no bounded route.
statement: For every finite nonabelian group $G$, the Gao constant satisfies $E(G)=\mathsf d(G)+|G|$, where $\mathsf d(G)$ is the largest integer $\ell$ for which there exists a product-one-free sequence over $G$ of length $\ell$, and $E(G)$ is the least integer $\ell$ such that every sequence over $G$ of length at least $\ell$ contains a product-one subsequence of length exactly $|G|$.
title: Zhuang–Gao conjecture

basis: A group-specific existence family of signed difference sets (v,k,lambda). He-Wu arXiv:2608.22936v2 settle 45,361 of the open cases plus three constructions. Individual cases are parameter instances; the full classification is open, with no full-scope mechanism.
statement: Given a finite abelian group $G$ of order $v$ and integers $k$ and $\lambda$, determine whether there exists a function $x:G\to\{-1,0,1\}$ such that $\sum_{g\in G}x(g)^2=k$ and, for every nonzero $h\in G$, $\sum_{g\in G}x(g)x(g+h)=\lambda$. Equivalently, determine which finite abelian groups admit a signed difference set with prescribed parameters $(v,k,\lambda)$.
title: Open group-specific existence problems for signed difference sets

basis: For all l>k>=2: ex(n,C_{2k+1}, C_{2k} cup {C_{2l+1}}) = o(n^2). Liu-Wu arXiv:2608.22893v1 prove an explicit O(n^{2-1/(k(k+1)(l-k))}) bound.
statement:
For all integers $l>k\ge 2$, let $\mathscr{C}_{2k}=\{C_3,C_4,\ldots,C_{2k}\}$. Then
$$\operatorname{ex}\bigl(n,C_{2k+1},\mathscr{C}_{2k}\cup\{C_{2l+1}\}\bigr)=o(n^2)\qquad\text{as }n\to\infty,$$
where $\operatorname{ex}(n,H,\mathcal{F})$ is the maximum number of copies of $H$ in an $n$-vertex graph containing no member of $\mathcal{F}$, and $C_i$ denotes the cycle of length $i$.
title: Gerbner–Győri–Methuku–Vizer generalized Turán conjecture

basis: For all r>=3, chi(F)=r and tw(F)>=r: ex(n,K_r,F) = Omega(n^{r-1}). Zhou-Yuan arXiv:2608.22742v1 refute it for every r>=3 with F_r=K_{r-3} join (subdivided K_4).
statement: For every integer $r\ge 3$ and every finite graph $F$ satisfying $\chi(F)=r$ and $\operatorname{tw}(F)\ge r$, there exist constants $c_F>0$ and $n_0(F)$ such that, for every integer $n\ge n_0(F)$, $\operatorname{ex}(n,K_r,F)\ge c_F n^{r-1}$, where $\operatorname{ex}(n,K_r,F)$ denotes the maximum number of copies of $K_r$ in an $n$-vertex $F$-free graph.
title: Gao–Wu–Xue treewidth conjecture for generalized Turán problems

basis: Equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis.
statement: Determine whether $\lambda^*(L)\ge 0$ for every $L>0$, where $\lambda^*(L)=\inf\left\{Q(f)/\lVert f\rVert_2^2:0\ne f,\ \operatorname{supp}f\subseteq[-L,L]\right\}$ and $Q$ is Weil’s quadratic form. Equivalently, determine whether $Q(f)\ge 0$ for every admissible compactly supported test function $f$; by Weil’s criterion, this is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis.
title: Riemann Hypothesis via Weil’s positivity criterion

basis: For all closed (M^n,g) with n>=7 and Q2,Q4,Q6>0, P6>0: P6 has a positive Green function. Gong-Li-Wei arXiv:2608.24148v1 give the counterexample S^2(1) x S^5(1/100).
statement: For every closed Riemannian manifold $(M^n,g)$ with $n\ge 7$, if $Q_g^{(2)}>0$, $Q_g^{(4)}>0$, $Q_g^{(6)}>0$, and the sixth-order GJMS operator $P_{6,g}$ is strictly positive as a self-adjoint operator, then $P_{6,g}$ has a positive Green function; equivalently, the associated sixth-order equation satisfies the strong maximum principle.
title: Strong maximum principle conjecture for higher-order GJMS operators

basis: For 3<=k<=n-1: K*_{n+k,n} = 4k(k-1). Zlatanov arXiv:2608.25805v1 proves only <=, and states the equality as its own conjecture. The matching lower bound needs an asymptotic ML-error analysis over all SNR-dependent codebooks; no tractable exact mechanism and a heavy formal burden.
statement: For every pair of integers $n,k$ satisfying $3\leq k\leq n-1$, the optimal leading coefficient in the high-SNR maximum-likelihood error-probability expansion for SNR-dependent $(n+k,n)$ AWGN spherical codes is conjectured to satisfy $K_{n+k,n}^{\ast}=4k(k-1)$, where $K_{n+k,n}^{\ast}$ denotes the SNR-wise optimal coefficient.
title: Optimal leading coefficient problem for AWGN spherical codes

basis: MB(complement P_n) for n>=8. Fei-Luo arXiv:2608.27227v1 prove MB=3 for every n>=6 with an explicit construction and a matching lower bound.
statement: For a graph $G$, let $\mathcal{S}(G)$ be the set of real symmetric matrices whose off-diagonal zero–nonzero pattern is the adjacency pattern of $G$. Define $MB(G)$ to be the minimum, over all $A\in\mathcal{S}(G)$ having exactly two distinct eigenvalues, of the smaller of their two multiplicities. Determine $MB(\overline{P_n})$ for every integer $n\ge 8$, where $P_n$ is the path on $n$ vertices.
title: Adm–Fallat–Meagher–Nasserasr–Plosker–Yang question on MB(\overline{P_n})

basis: Max number of real circles tangent to three general conics. The conjectured 136 is disproved by Brysiewicz arXiv:2609.01521v1 (144). The exact maximum (at most the complex count) is open and hard.
statement: Determine the maximum number of distinct real circles tangent to each of three general real conics in the Euclidean plane. The proposed conjecture was that every such triple has at most $136$ real tritangent circles, with an explicit configuration attaining $136$; the 2026 preprint claims a configuration with $144$.
title: Maximum number of circles tangent to three conics

basis: For every odd m>=5: f(m)=ceil((2m-1)/3). Lin-You arXiv:2609.00944v2 settle this for all sufficiently large odd m. No effective threshold appears in the abstract; the small-m residual is not a bounded-certificate target.
statement: For an odd integer $m\ge 3$, determine the least integer $f(m)$ such that, for every integer $n\ge f(m)$ and every tree $T_n$ on $n$ vertices, the Ramsey number satisfies $R(T_n,C_m)=2n-1$. The conjectured exact value is $f(m)=\left\lceil\frac{2m-1}{3}\right\rceil$ for every odd $m\ge 5$.
title: Ramsey threshold for trees versus odd cycles
